title: Withdraw statistics_target escalation; test planner cost recalibration instead
configuration_cause: default_statistics_target=300 was accepted on a single lucky replicate (30.4% gain) while the second replicate gained only 0.52%; the frozen p50/p95 decrease predictions were refuted in both blocks, so finer histograms are not the lever. GetUserTweets still consumes 88% of terminal capacity at p50=175us with an Index Scan plan, so the residual cost is per-call index descent and heap fetch, not selectivity estimation.
mechanism: The r006 statistics escalation is withdrawn: it produced no reproducible latency reduction and its mechanism verdict is refuted. The dominant GetUserTweets path is already an Index Scan at estimated cost 8.45 with estimated_rows=1, so the remaining per-call cost is index descent plus heap tuple visibility checks. Lowering random_page_cost from 1.5 to 1.1 and seq_page_cost from 0.8 to 0.7 keeps the planner firmly on the index path while making the cost model consistent with a fully cached working set (2TB RAM, shared_buffers=512MB, zero io_waiting_backends), which prevents any marginal plan flip to a seq scan on skewed user_id values and stabilizes the hot path's per-call cost.
query_effect: GetUserTweets retains its Index Scan plan; the cost model no longer over-penalizes the cached random index descent, so no plan flip to sequential scan occurs on skewed user_id predicates and per-call latency stays at or below the incumbent p50.
expected_tps_effect: Neutral-to-slightly-positive: stabilizing the dominant transaction's plan removes variance-driven tail stalls; expected +0.3% to +1.0% successful TPS, not a large jump.
expected_latency_effect: GetUserTweets p50 unchanged or marginally lower; p95 unchanged within noise. No regression expected on InsertTweet.

predictions.rationale: Cached-cost model keeps the hot index path stable and avoids marginal seq-scan flips on skewed user_id values.
Tail is dominated by WAL/commit path, not planner choice; expect no material p95 movement.
Stabilizing the 88%-capacity transaction frees terminal time for additional completions.

alternatives.statement: default_statistics_target is already past its useful plateau at 300; further increases add ANALYZE cost with no plan change because the hot query is a single-row index lookup.
The residual GetUserTweets cost is commit-path WAL sync (sync_average_ms 0.137, wal_waiting_backends max 1), so only the WAL commit-path bundle can move TPS; planner cost knobs will be neutral.

why_exceeds_incumbent: The incumbent's accepted gain rests on one 30.4% replicate against a 0.52% replicate, and both frozen latency predictions were refuted. Recalibrating random_page_cost/seq_page_cost to the measured fully-cached regime is a low-risk, mechanism-consistent adjustment that protects the dominant index path without repeating the refuted statistics escalation.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Lower from 1.5 to 1.1 within safe [1.0,6.0]; measured zero io_waiting_backends and 2TB RAM mean random index reads are cache-resident, so cost should approach seq_page_cost.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: planner cost of cached random index descent on the hot GetUserTweets path

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Lower from 0.8 to 0.7 within safe [0.5,2.0]; keeps the random/seq ratio near 1.57 so the index path stays preferred without over-penalizing cached heap fetches.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: I/O cost scale paired with random_page_cost to preserve index-path preference

nodes.label: Cache-consistent cost model keeps GetUserTweets on stable Index Scan path

cross_domain_requirements: WAL commit-path bundle (commit_delay/commit_siblings/wal_writer_flush_after) remains the memory_storage nomination; planner cost change is orthogonal and additive.
